lonja-seda.title: Silk Exchange
lonja-seda.summary: One of the finest works of European civil Gothic.
lonja-seda.description: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996, La Lonja was the setting for the transactions that made Valencia the largest trading port in the western Mediterranean. Its Hall of Columns, with spiral pillars that look like stone palm trees, is one of the most photographed spaces in the city.
info: Plaça del Mercat, s/n · Ciutat Vella

catedral-caliz.title: Cathedral & Holy Grail
catedral-caliz.summary: 13th-century Gothic cathedral that houses the Holy Grail.
catedral-caliz.description: The Chapel of the Holy Chalice houses one of the most valuable relics in the Christian world: the cup that, according to tradition, Jesus used at the Last Supper. The Cathedral celebrates the Third Holy Chalice Jubilee Year until 29 October 2026. From the Micalet bell tower (207 steps) you can see the whole city.
info: Plaça de la Reina, s/n · Ciutat Vella

mercado-central.title: Central Market
mercado-central.detailEyebrow: Historic centre · Asset of Cultural Interest
mercado-central.summary: The largest fresh produce market in Europe.
mercado-central.description: The largest fresh produce market in Europe. A Modernista cathedral of iron, stained glass and tiles where the aromas of the huerta and the Mediterranean have filled every corner since 1928.
info: Mon–Sat 7:30–15:00 · closed Sundays and public holidays
Plaça de la Ciutat de Bruges · Ciutat Vella
Xàtiva metro (L3, L5, L9) · 5 min on foot from La Lonja

barrio-carmen.title: El Carmen district
barrio-carmen.summary: The oldest and most bohemian quarter in Valencia.
barrio-carmen.description: The oldest, most bohemian and most vibrant quarter in Valencia. A unique cocktail of medieval walls, street art, avant-garde museums and squares full of Mediterranean life. The Serranos Towers (1392–1398) and the Quart Towers can be visited free of charge all year round.
info: Bus 28 and 94 · 10 min on foot from the Cathedral

oceanografic.title: Oceanogràfic
oceanografic.description: 110,000 m² and 42 million litres of salt water. Europe’s biggest aquarium brings together the world’s most important marine ecosystems, the longest underwater tunnel on the continent and the only family of beluga whales in Europe. Opened on 14 February 2003.
info: From €33 · book online with a discount

albufera.title: La Albufera Natural Park
albufera.summary: Spain’s largest lake and the birthplace of paella.
albufera.description: Just 15 minutes from Valencia, nature in its purest state: a Ramsar site, a natural park since 1986 and the most spectacular sunset in the Mediterranean. A boat trip is the most complete experience; autumn, with the rice fields ripe and the highest concentration of birds, is the most special time.
info: Free access · boat jetties from 9:00 to sunset
El Palmar and El Saler · 10 km to the south

iglesia-san-nicolas.title: Church of San Nicolás
iglesia-san-nicolas.description: Almost 2,000 m² of Baroque frescoes designed by Palomino cover a 15th-century Gothic structure in the most surprising monument in the historic centre. There is a multimedia projection every hour from 11:00; arrive 10 minutes early to get the best spot.

jardin-turia.title: Turia Gardens
jardin-turia.summary: Spain’s largest urban park, 9 km without cars.
jardin-turia.description: 9 kilometres of green park that cross Valencia from west to east along the old bed of its river. It links the Parque de Cabecera and the Bioparc with the City of Arts and Sciences and never closes: it is the city’s open-air gym and green lung. Valencia was European Green Capital in 2024.
info: Old bed of the Turia river · from Cabecera to the City of Arts
Valenbisi and cycle lane · Alameda metro (L3, L5)

la-marina.title: La Marina
la-marina.description: A former port reinvented, where the avant-garde architecture of the Veles e Vents, the historic Tinglados warehouses and the Clock Building sit alongside more than 15 restaurants with sea views and around 40 water-sports companies. Access is completely free.
info: Marina Real Juan Carlos I · Seaside districts
Tram L4 and L6 · bus 4 and 30

mestalla.title: Mestalla
mestalla.description: The black-and-white coliseum, opened in 1923: the oldest stadium in Spanish top-flight football, with over a hundred years of history and home to Valencia CF. Whether or not you are a fan, the stadium and museum tour is one of the most recommended in Valencia.
info: Tours 10:00–18:00 · no tours on match days
From €12 · buy online to avoid queues

museo-bellas-artes.title: Fine Arts Museum
museo-bellas-artes.summary: The second most important art gallery in Spain.
museo-bellas-artes.description: From Valencian Gothic to Sorolla, taking in Velázquez, Goya, El Greco, Botticelli and Van Dyck, in a 17th-century Baroque palace beside the Turia Gardens. Admission is completely free.
info: C/ San Pío V, 9 · beside the Turia Gardens

playas.title: Valencia beaches
playas.summary: 19.5 km of golden sand and 8 Blue Flags.
playas.description: From El Cabanyal to La Devesa, from the liveliest seafront promenade in Spain to the unspoilt dunes of La Albufera Natural Park. Valencia is one of the few big cities where you can go to the beach by metro: line L4 drops you at Les Arenes and bus 19 reaches Malvarrosa.
info: Paseo de Neptuno · Las Arenas beach
Tram L4 (Les Arenes) · bus 19 to Malvarrosa

ruzafa.title: Ruzafa
ruzafa.summary: The most vibrant neighbourhood in Valencia.
ruzafa.description: From a 9th-century Arab garden to the epicentre of signature cuisine, contemporary art and the city’s most creative nightlife. A multicultural neighbourhood where long-established bars compete with restaurants run by Michelin-starred chefs. It has no visiting hours: it works at any time of day.
info: No set hours · from the morning snack to the last drink
C/ Cádiz and surrounding streets · Eixample
Xàtiva and Bailén metro · 10 min on foot

bioparc.title: Bioparc
bioparc.summary: A piece of Africa in Valencia.
bioparc.description: More than 6,000 animals of 150 species in 100,000 m² of African habitats where the barriers are practically invisible. A new-generation zoo on the banks of the old Turia riverbed.
info: Av. Pío Baroja, 3 · Parque de Cabecera
Metro L3 and L5 · Nou d’Octubre or Av. del Cid

cac.title: City of Arts and Sciences
cac.summary: Six unique buildings along almost two kilometres of the old Turia riverbed.
cac.description: Designed by Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela, it combines interactive science, Europe’s largest aquarium, 3D cinema and an opera house (Palau de les Arts). We recommend spending a full day there and buying tickets online.
info: Depends on the venue · check opening times online
Metro L3, L5, L7 and L9 · Alameda · 15 min through the Turia Gardens

paella.title: Paella valenciana
paella.description: The most international dish of Valencian gastronomy: our contribution to world cuisine. Born in La Albufera in the 18th century, it is today the gastronomic symbol of Valencia. It is cooked over a wood fire, with chicken, rabbit, garrofón beans and green beans, and eaten straight from the pan.
info: El Palmar and La Albufera · Malvarrosa and the seafront
It is a lunchtime dish: book ahead in summer

fideua.title: Fideuà
fideua.description: Born by accident on a boat in Grau de Gandia, fideuà is paella’s seafaring cousin: same technique, same fire, same ritual, but with noodles instead of rice. It is served with alioli.
info: Restaurants in El Grau and along the seafront

arroz-horno.title: Arròs al forn
arroz-horno.summary: The great unknown of Valencian cuisine.
arroz-horno.description: The dish Valencians keep for themselves. Born from the stew pot and the baker’s oven, arròs al forn is the most authentic, hearty and homely face of rice cooking.
info: Traditional eateries in the centre and Ruzafa

arroz-negro.title: Arròs negre
arroz-negro.summary: The most mysterious rice in Valencia.
arroz-negro.description: Black as the sea at night. Cuttlefish ink stains every grain of rice and concentrates the flavour of the Mediterranean in a dish that surprises as much for its look as for its taste.
info: Restaurants at the port and in La Marina

all-i-pebre.title: All i pebre
all-i-pebre.summary: The dish of the fishermen of La Albufera.
all-i-pebre.description: Garlic and paprika. The eel stew of the fishermen of La Albufera, which rivals Valencian paella in history and tradition. Catarroja, El Palmar and the lake where it was born.

esgarraet.title: Esgarraet
esgarraet.summary: The best-kept secret of Valencian cuisine.
esgarraet.description: Four ingredients, your hands and patience: the contrast between salt cod and the sweetness of roasted pepper. A traditional Easter tapa that is enjoyed all year round.
info: Tapas bars in El Carmen and around the Central Market

arroz-senyoret.title: Arròs del senyoret
arroz-senyoret.description: All the seafood peeled: no shells and no mess. Prawns, squid, cuttlefish and monkfish, all cleaned, on a fish stock and salmorreta base, where convenience is the luxury.
info: Restaurants in Malvarrosa and La Marina

bunyol.title: Bunyols de carabassa
bunyol.summary: The most Fallas dessert in Valencia.
bunyol.description: The smell that defines the Fallas of Valencia. Fluffy inside, crisp outside, rolled in sugar and served with hot chocolate: the most Valencian sweet treat.
info: Street stalls in March and fritter shops in the centre

horchata.title: Horchata and fartons
horchata.summary: The most Valencian drink in the world.
horchata.description: White, cold, creamy and sweet. Horchata made from tiger nuts from Alboraya is the liquid gold of Valencia: lactose-free, gluten-free and with a Designation of Origin. It is drunk with fartons for dipping.
info: Horchata bars in Alboraya and the centre

fallas.title: Fallas 2027
fallas.summary: 19 days of gunpowder, ephemeral art, flowers and fire.
fallas.description: 19 days of gunpowder, ephemeral art, flowers and fire. Valencia’s biggest festival combines satire, tradition and the most impressive pyrotechnic spectacle in Europe.
info: Plaza del Ayuntamiento and every neighbourhood of Valencia

corpus-christi.title: Corpus Christi
corpus-christi.summary: Valencia’s Great Festival since the 14th century.
corpus-christi.description: A historic procession, medieval dances, the eleven Rocas pulled by horses and the fight between Virtue and the Seven Deadly Sins. It takes place 60 days after Easter.

gran-feria.title: Gran Feria de Julio
gran-feria.summary: A whole month of festivities in high summer.
gran-feria.description: Concerts under the stars in Viveros, fireworks every Saturday, the Jazz Festival, the Band Competition and the Battle of Flowers. All of July, since 1871.

festivales-verano.title: Summer festivals
festivales-verano.summary: Nine festivals from April to September 2026.
festivales-verano.description: Nine festivals that turn the Comunitat Valenciana into the musical epicentre of the Mediterranean every summer. From urban indie to reggae, from the beach to the CAC, from techno to big international names.

festivos.title: Public holidays calendar
festivos.summary: 14 public holidays: national, regional and local.
festivos.description: The full calendar of non-working days in the city of Valencia for 2026, with the traditions and celebrations of each date.
info: Many museums and markets close on public holidays: check the opening hours

deportes.title: Sports
deportes.summary: Valencia, city of running, cycling and the sea.
deportes.description: The Mediterranean climate, 9 kilometres of linear park, 20 km of beach and 160 km of cycle lanes make Valencia the ideal destination for sport all year round. Marathon, popular races, sailing and much more.
info: All year · the Valencia Marathon is on 6 December
Register for the Marathon well in advance: it sells out in hours

aloj-centro.title: Historic centre
aloj-centro.description: Four options for every budget in the heart of the city, a few steps from the Cathedral, the Central Market and La Lonja de la Seda.

aloj-gran-via.title: Gran Vía district
aloj-gran-via.description: Grand avenues with Modernista buildings, the Turia Gardens at the door and the best food district in the city a step away.
info: Gran Vía Marqués del Turia · L’Eixample

aloj-ruzafa.title: Ruzafa district
aloj-ruzafa.description: The most creative and cosmopolitan neighbourhood in Valencia: art galleries, design bars, world cuisine and the energy of a neighbourhood that never stops. 10 minutes on foot from everything.
info: C/ Cádiz and surrounding streets · Eixample

aloj-cac.title: City of Arts and Sciences
aloj-cac.summary: Four hotels facing Valencia’s most iconic landmark.
aloj-cac.description: The Oceanogràfic, the Palau de les Arts and the Museu de les Ciències on your doorstep, with the Turia Gardens as a walk to the centre.
info: Av. de França · City of Arts and Sciences

aloj-playa.title: Beach area and seafront promenade
aloj-playa.description: From the great historic luxury resort to the boutique hotel with Sorolla’s light and the family classic with history since 1916.
info: Paseo de Neptuno · Las Arenas beach

aloj-barato-exclusivo.title: From luxury to budget
aloj-barato-exclusivo.summary: Exclusive and budget hotels, all well located.
aloj-barato-exclusivo.description: From historic seafront luxury to the best budget options. Exclusive and affordable hotels, all well located.
info: Book ahead for Fallas and in summer

albufera-barca.title: La Albufera by boat
albufera-barca.summary: Electric boat trip on the lake.
albufera-barca.description: The boat trip is the most complete way to get to know La Albufera: electric boats, bilingual guides and the best light of the day at sunset, among rice fields and migratory birds.
info: El Palmar · 11 km from the centre

ecoturismo.title: Ecotourism
ecoturismo.description: Valencia is much more than city and beach: 21,000 hectares of Albufera, more than 300 bird species and four natural parks a step from the centre. Signposted, flat trails, observatories and visitor centres.
info: Autumn, with the rice fields ripe, is the best time for birds

muevete.title: Getting around Valencia
muevete.area: Public transport, Valenbisi and pedestrian areas
muevete.summary: Public transport, Valenbisi and pedestrian areas
muevete.description: Almost 200 km of cycle lanes, flat terrain, metro and tram to the beach and a Turia Gardens free of cars. The city is best explored on foot, by bike or on public transport.
info: Valenbisi: weekly pass for visitors at any station

viaje-responsable.title: Responsible travel
viaje-responsable.area: Positive impact on the local community
viaje-responsable.summary: Positive impact on the local community
viaje-responsable.description: Being a responsible tourist in Valencia takes no effort: it is small everyday decisions that add up. These are the commitments you can adopt during your stay.

comercio-local.title: Local shops
comercio-local.description: Neighbourhood markets, long-established shops and small local businesses: buying here is the most direct way to make sure tourism leaves value in the city.
info: Markets open in the morning: go early

consejos.title: Tips for travelling better
consejos.description: A practical guide with tips to reduce your footprint while travelling: water, energy, waste and respect for natural spaces.
info: Bring a reusable bottle: there are fountains all over the city

viaje-sostenible.title: Sustainable and smart city
viaje-sostenible.description: Valencia is not just sustainable: it is smart. European Green Capital 2024 and European Capital of Smart Tourism 2022, the city combines technology, nature and culture for better travel.
info: European Green Capital 2024 and European Capital of Smart Tourism 2022

albufera-barca.title: Boat trip on La Albufera
albufera-barca.description: Tour the lake in an electric boat with a bilingual guide, among rice fields and migratory birds.

taller-paella.title: Valencian paella workshop
taller-paella.description: Learn to cook an authentic Valencian paella with a local chef. Ingredients and tasting included.

kayak-albufera.title: Kayaking on La Albufera
kayak-albufera.description: Kayak route along the canals of the Natural Park at dawn. Guide, kayak and life jacket included.

excursion-albufera-paella.title: La Albufera excursion with paella
excursion-albufera-paella.description: Visit to the Natural Park with a boat trip and a traditional paella lunch included.

paddle-surf.title: Paddle surfing at Las Arenas
paddle-surf.description: Beginner paddle surf lesson in the Mediterranean with a qualified instructor. Equipment included.

taller-horchata.title: Horchata and fartons workshop
taller-horchata.description: Learn to make traditional tiger-nut horchata and fartons in this unique workshop in Valencia.

tour-ruzafa.title: Ruzafa tour: art and food
tour-ruzafa.description: Discover Valencia’s trendiest neighbourhood with tastings in its best bars and visits to art galleries.

ruta-ciutat-vella.title: Guided walk through Ciutat Vella
ruta-ciutat-vella.description: A guided walk through El Carmen, La Lonja, the Central Market and Plaza del Ayuntamiento with an official guide.

visita-catedral.title: Guided visit to the Cathedral
visita-catedral.description: Discover the Cathedral’s secrets: the Holy Chalice, the Gothic chapel and the views from the Micalet.

tour-lonja-catedral.title: La Lonja de la Seda and the Cathedral
tour-lonja-catedral.description: A combined visit to the two great monuments of the historic centre with a bilingual guide.

tour-ciudad-artes.title: City of Arts and Sciences tour
tour-ciudad-artes.description: Guided visit to Calatrava’s complex with admission to the Museu de les Ciències and L’Hemisfèric included.

ruta-bici.title: Bike ride around Valencia
ruta-bici.description: Pedal through the Turia Gardens, the beaches and the City of Arts. Bike included.

tour-carmen-nocturno.title: Night tour of El Carmen
tour-carmen-nocturno.description: A night-time walk through Valencia’s most bohemian neighbourhood: street art, historic bars and medieval legends.

tourist-card-72.title: Valencia Tourist Card 72 h
tourist-card-72.description: The card that opens up the whole of Valencia: free transport, 14 museums included, a free tapa and discounts of up to 50% on more than 130 tourist services.

bus-turistico.title: Valencia Tourist Bus
bus-turistico.description: The double-decker tourist bus, 100% electric, runs through the 17 key points of Valencia. Hop on and off whenever you like for 24 or 48 hours.

entrada-oceanografic.title: Oceanogràfic ticket
entrada-oceanografic.description: Admission to Europe’s largest aquarium with the dolphinarium show included. Avoid queues by buying online.
